prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I keep the round-1 configuration: a single B020 part naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific chain is complete and independently confirmed: proglucagon processing and human incretin physiology (Holst), identification and synthesis of the biologically active GLP-1 peptide (Mojsov), and receptor biology, GLP-2 and translation (Drucker). Randomized outcome trials show glycemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal benefit, and the field is mature. The round-1 exchange did not change my view of the science, and nobody argued that maturity is in doubt. What it did sharpen is the framing. The three names are justified as a prize for how the biology was discovered, and I would state that plainly in the citation instead of letting the drug-development question be settled by default. I have not moved again since round 1, when I left my opening trio (Drucker, Holst, Knudsen) for this one.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point. Habener sits outside the credited names, and from the supplied record I cannot show that Mojsov's identification of the active peptide stands against his group's claim. Knudsen's long-acting analogue chemistry is what made the physiology usable, and omitting it can be read as honouring the idea and not the drug. I also still think a single-achievement prize narrows the committee's range, since B045 and B040 are serious candidates. But a second part would force dropping a core GLP-1 name under the three-person limit, and I do not think that cost is justified. Long-term safety and durability of the obesity indication are still accumulating, as Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius say. I treat that as a reason for careful citation wording, not for delay, because the benefit in diabetes and cardiovascular and renal outcomes is already established.

responses.point: In round 1 Svenningsson named Mojsov, Holst and Drucker as the most defensible trio and fell back to a therapy-centred configuration if the committee judges that the therapeutic achievement is the point. The chair also asks whether the citation should honour discovery only or drug development as well.
responses.response: We now name the same trio, so the open question is the principle behind it. I would honour discovery and physiology only, and say so in the citation. If the committee instead decides the achievement is the therapy, Knudsen should come in, but I would then want to say which of Mojsov and Drucker leaves and why. I do not think Mojsov is the obvious one to drop, because the active peptide is the step that made the physiology tractable. Drucker would be the harder case, since his receptor and translational work links the physiology to the drug. That is why I prefer to settle the principle first and not edit the trio around it. On safety and durability of the obesity indication, I agree it belongs in the committee's thinking. I would reflect it in measured citation wording, with 'enabled' and not claims of cure, and not in delaying a prize on a mechanism that is already well confirmed.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius says that credit in B020 is not clean and that we should test attribution as hard as we test the science. She also holds B034 (TNF blockade) as her first fallback.
responses.response: I agree on testing attribution as hard as the science, and that is how I tried to arrive at the trio. Her own case helps: each of the three covers a separate, checkable step, with Holst on physiology, Mojsov on the active peptide and Drucker on biology and translation. The weak step is still the peptide, where Habener is outside the supplied names. On B034, my round-1 doubt was whether the contribution goes beyond clinical validation. Her reply that the path from mechanism to patients is exceptionally clear, with a clean Feldmann and Maini pair, moves me to treat it as a serious candidate and not as proof of concept only. It does not move me above B045 or B040 as a fallback, because TNF cloning and antibody engineering credit outside the names remains open, and she says she cannot fully resolve it either. If she can show from the record that Feldmann and Maini first established TNF as the dominant upstream cytokine, that would change my ordering.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks optogenetics (B045) second as a transformative circuit-dissection method, proposes Boyden, Nagel and Deisseroth, and admits that six-way credit is contested. He also holds that B020 alone honours the mechanism and leaves drug engineering as a later contribution.
responses.response: I agree that the GLP-1 trio honours the mechanism, and I accept his framing of drug engineering as a distinct later step. On B045 I part company with the proposed trio. Dropping Bamberg, Hegemann, Miesenboeck or others to reach three is the very reduction the chair asks us to defend, and I do not think we can defend it from this record. Nagel and Hegemann's channelrhodopsin work and Bamberg's earlier photocurrent work are the molecular discovery, while Boyden and Deisseroth made it a neuronal tool. That is a different allocation from his, and no three-name split honours both layers. Early clinical translation is also still limited, which counts against B045 as a prize now. I keep it as an alternative on the strength of the science, and I do not think it can sit beside B020 under the three-person cap.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks the unfolded protein response (B052) second, calling it conceptually original with a clean Mori and Walter attribution. He also doubts that a B052 part can sit beside B020 without cutting the GLP-1 trio.
responses.response: I agree with his arithmetic. Any two-part prize that includes B020 forces a three-person total, so one of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov would have to go, and each is the sole owner of a discovery step. That rules out a combined prize for me. On B052 I accept that its attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist and that the pathway is mechanistically complete. My remaining reservation is the disease link. The relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer is plausible but its therapeutic payoff is still mostly prospective, and the Nobel tradition has honoured basic mechanism before. I read it as a strong candidate for a later year and not a competitor to GLP-1 now. That is why it is not among my two alternatives, which are B045 and B040.

responses.point: Linnarsson, who ranks CAR-T (B040) second, proposes only June and Sadelain and doubts that Rosenberg's contribution to the CAR work is decisive. He notes that Eshhar's omission limits any fair configuration.
responses.response: His pairing is cleaner than a trio with Rosenberg, and I take the Eshhar concern as seriously as he does. The chair asks whether credit can be assigned fairly without Eshhar. I do not think it can be settled from the supplied record. Eshhar introduced the chimeric receptor concept, which comes before the June and Sadelain constructs. A June and Sadelain pair would therefore need a citation limited to the clinical CAR-T constructs, and even then it could be challenged. Rosenberg's adoptive transfer and gene-modified lymphocyte work is a real precursor, so I would not remove him just to make the pair fit. That is why B040 stays an alternative. If the committee ever moved to it, I would favour June and Sadelain only after the committee has explicitly weighed Eshhar's claim.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1 peptide stands against Habener's claim cannot be resolved from the supplied record. If the committee finds it unresolved, the citation should say 'identification of its active form' as a field-level description and not assign priority.

Whether the committee honours discovery and physiology only or also drug development. If it chooses development, Knudsen would need to replace Mojsov or Drucker, and I have no clear reason to prefer either replacement.
Whether long-term safety and durability of the obesity indication should affect citation wording or timing. I judge wording only.
For B045, whether any of the six credited names can be dropped without unfair allocation, and for B040 whether Eshhar's claim can be set aside fairly. Neither is resolved by the record.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I have co-authored with colleagues (Linnarsson and Frisen) and share the Karolinska Institutet setting, but none of the shortlisted candidates is a documented collaborator, mentor or KI colleague, so no recusal appears warranted. This is unchanged since round 1.
